reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, let μ be a probability measure on E, and let C be a positive real number. Suppose that for every smooth compactly supported real-valued function v on E, the integral of v² log(v²) minus the integral of v² times the logarithm of that integral is at most 2C times the integral of the squared norm of the gradient of v. Then for every smooth compactly supported real-valued function g on E, the integral of the square of g minus its μ-mean, where the subtraction is taken before squaring, is at most C times the integral of the squared norm of the gradient of g. All integrals are with respect to μ, and logarithms at zero are interpreted as zero.
objects: The space E, the probability measure μ, the real constant C, the test functions v and g, and their Riesz gradients.
domains: E is a complete real inner-product space of finite real dimension with its Borel measurable structure. The functions v and g map E to ℝ. All integrals are real Bochner integrals over E with respect to μ.
quantifiers: For every such E, every probability measure μ on E, and every C > 0: if the premise holds for every smooth compactly supported v : E → ℝ, the conclusion holds for every smooth compactly supported g : E → ℝ.
assumptions: μ has total mass one and C is strictly positive. For each infinitely continuously differentiable v whose nonzero set has compact closure, ∫ v² log(v²) dμ − (∫ v² dμ) log(∫ v² dμ) ≤ 2C ∫ ‖∇v‖² dμ. The logarithm is totalized by log(0) = 0, so the product q log(q) at zero is zero.
conclusion: For each infinitely continuously differentiable g whose nonzero set has compact closure, ∫ (g(x) − ∫ g(y) dμ(y))² dμ(x) ≤ C ∫ ‖∇g‖² dμ.
scopes: The space, measure and positive constant are fixed across the implication. The universal quantifier over v belongs wholly to the premise; the universal quantifier over g belongs wholly to the conclusion. The inner integral in y is the μ-mean of g and is independent of the outer variable x; it is subtracted from g(x) before squaring. Neither function is required to be normalized or to have zero mean.
constant_dependencies: The same supplied C appears in both inequalities: the coefficient is 2C in the premise and C in the conclusion. C is independent of the test functions; no additional factor or claim of optimality is asserted.
